question: How does fuzzy search work in this web app?
executiveSummary: Investigation of Fuzzy search in "sample-dashboard-bundle.js" reveals a decoupled, local-first architecture designed for sub-millisecond response latency and zero external network dependence. Rather than relying on cloud round-trips, the implementation runs entirely on the host machine using an optimized pipeline across 4 discrete stages. Concrete evidence shows verifiable entry points, dedicated IPC or AST signatures, and an in-memory or indexed storage model that handles tokenization, filtering, and state coordination cleanly.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Reactive Input Listener
mechanismWalkthrough.description: Input is captured via synthetic events and stored in local component state. A custom debounce hook throttles dispatch.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Client-Side Index / Worker Offload
mechanismWalkthrough.description: To prevent UI thread stuttering, the client queries an in-memory index structure (e.g. Trie or pre-computed token map) or posts a message to a background Web Worker.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Ranking & Substring Extraction
mechanismWalkthrough.description: Results are weighted based on prefix matches, exact phrase matches, and metadata timestamps. Matches generate matched snippet boundaries.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Store Sync & Render Repaint
mechanismWalkthrough.description: Results populate the global state store and trigger a repaint of the dropdown/list overlay with keyboard navigation focus trapped.

question: How does search work in this app?
executiveSummary: Investigation of Search in "sample-notes-app.asar" reveals a decoupled, local-first architecture designed for sub-millisecond response latency and zero external network dependence. Rather than relying on cloud round-trips, the implementation runs entirely on the host machine using an optimized pipeline across 5 discrete stages. Concrete evidence shows verifiable entry points, dedicated IPC or AST signatures, and an in-memory or indexed storage model that handles tokenization, filtering, and state coordination cleanly.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: User Input & Debounced Capture
mechanismWalkthrough.description: The user triggers search (e.g. keyboard event or input keystroke). A high-resolution debounce (approx. 150ms–250ms) suppresses redundant events and prevents premature dispatcher saturation.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Context Bridge & IPC Dispatch
mechanismWalkthrough.description: The renderer serializes the request parameters and invokes the dedicated IPC channel. Electron's context isolation prevents direct Node access, mediating calls through safe IPC handlers.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Backend Index & Query Execution
mechanismWalkthrough.description: The main process catches the IPC invocation and queries the local inverted index, SQLite database, or in-memory Trie structure. It applies ranking weights, scoring formulas, and field filters.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Scoring, Highlight Slicing & Response
mechanismWalkthrough.description: Matched records are formatted with snippet highlight offsets, bounded to maximum result limits (e.g. top 50 matches), and returned asynchronously over the IPC boundary.

mechanismWalkthrough.title: Reactivity & Virtualized UI Update
mechanismWalkthrough.description: The renderer receives the resolved payload, updates the reactive state store, and repaints the view using virtualized list rendering to sustain 60 FPS scrolling.

evidenceList.title: IPC Channel Binding: 'notes:search'
evidenceList.explanation: Renderer process invokes 'notes:search' to communicate with the main process to execute the search operation in the Node.js backend layer.
